Conflicting opinions and research outcomes — The retrieved evidence contains directly opposing claims: some sources state identical twins are genetically identical [d1, d8, d12, d14], while others state they are not, citing genetic differences [d3, d4, d6, d9, d11].

The answer to whether identical twins are genetically identical depends on the scientific perspective considered. Traditional sources state that identical twins, originating from a single fertilized egg, share the same genetic information and have the same genome [d1, d8, d12, d14]. However, recent research findings indicate that identical twins are not perfectly identical, as they accumulate genetic mutations early in development, leading to an average of 5.2 genetic differences and meaning they do not share 100% of their DNA [d3, d4, d9, d11]. This conflict in the evidence reflects ongoing scientific debate and evolving understanding in genetics.
